title: Restore Admin button and collection creation in production

requirements.summary: Ensure the Admin navigation link is always rendered for authenticated admin users without being silently hidden in production builds
acceptanceCriteria: When logged in as an admin, the Admin link is visible in the navigation bar in the live/production deployment.
Clicking the Admin link routes to the AdminDashboard page.
Non-admin users do not see the Admin link.

file_operations.description: Review and fix the conditional logic that renders the Admin link. Ensure that when useIsCallerAdminWithTimeout confirms admin status (phase === 'confirmed' && isAdmin === true), the Admin link is unconditionally rendered. Remove any production-specific conditionals or environment checks that could suppress the link. Verify the retry button is shown when phase === 'timeout' or phase === 'error'. Ensure the loading state correctly prevents flickering during the admin check.

requirements.summary: Ensure the AdminDashboard page renders the collection creation form and NFT management tabs correctly in production without environment-specific code paths preventing UI from loading
acceptanceCriteria: The AdminDashboard page displays the Collections tab with the ability to create a new collection via AdminCollectionForm.
The AdminDashboard page displays the NFTs tab with the ability to create/edit NFTs via AdminNFTForm.
The admin dashboard works identically in both draft and live deployments.

file_operations.description: Audit the AdminDashboard component to ensure no environment-specific conditionals or build-time flags prevent the UI from rendering in production. Verify that the phase-based rendering logic correctly shows the dashboard content when phase === 'confirmed' && isAdmin === true. Ensure the Tabs component with Collections and NFTs tabs is always rendered for confirmed admins. Remove any dead code paths or debug-only conditionals that could cause discrepancies between draft and live deployments.

Review the AdminCollectionForm to ensure it renders and submits correctly in production. Verify that the form state, validation, and mutation hooks work identically in both environments. Check for any hardcoded environment checks or feature flags that could disable form functionality in production.

Review the AdminNFTForm to ensure it renders and submits correctly in production. Verify that image upload, collection selection, and mutation hooks work identically in both draft and live environments. Check for any environment-specific logic that could prevent the form from functioning in production.

requirements.summary: Audit and fix the useIsCallerAdminWithTimeout and useIsCallerAdmin hooks to ensure admin status is correctly detected without premature timeouts in production
acceptanceCriteria: Admin status check completes successfully on the live deployment without prematurely hitting the timeout phase.
If the admin check fails or times out, a retry button is shown rather than silently hiding the Admin link.
Console errors related to admin status detection are resolved.

file_operations.description: Review and fix the timeout logic to ensure the 20-second timeout is appropriate for production network conditions. Verify that the hook correctly transitions between phases (checking → confirmed/timeout/error) and that the backend method checkIsAdmin is called correctly. Ensure proper error handling for network failures and that the retry function resets state correctly. Add console logging for debugging phase transitions if not already present.

Review the useIsCallerAdmin hook to ensure it correctly calls the backend isCallerAdmin method and handles responses properly. Verify that the query is enabled only when the actor is ready and the user is authenticated. Check for any race conditions or caching issues that could cause stale admin status in production.

Verify that the actor initialization and admin token handling work correctly in production. Ensure that the actor is properly cached and that dependent queries are invalidated when the actor changes. Check that the access control initialization does not interfere with subsequent admin status checks. Review any environment-specific configuration that could affect actor availability in production.
